### Full Report Content:
```markdown
# Nitrosend CLI first-run report

- **Environment.** macOS (darwin arm64), Node.js `v22.14.0`, npm `11.13.0`, `@nitrosend/cli` `0.3.9`. I ran the CLI through `npx` rather than a global install; the npx package cache was created at `2026-10-21T20:15:58Z`.
- **Commands.** First `npx --yes @nitrosend/cli whoami --json` at `2026-10-21T20:16:22Z`, then `npx --yes @nitrosend/cli send --to proof@dogfood.nitrosend.net --subject "<short transactional subject>" --body "<one-line plain-text body>" --trace` at `2026-10-21T20:16:44Z`.
- **Result and timing.** The message was created at `20:16:41.702Z` and sent at `20:16:44.432Z`; install-to-first-send was about 46 seconds. `whoami` returned the active profile and the send exited successfully.
- **Slowest step.** The CLI itself was quick. The slower part was the earlier sender setup: the account existed at `2026-10-21T07:18:32Z` and the hosted sender was verified at `07:18:44Z`, well before this CLI run.
- **Defect or doc gap.** No blocking defect. One doc gap: the README shows `npm install -g @nitrosend/cli`, but not the shorter `npx --yes @nitrosend/cli ...` path. Repro: `npx --yes @nitrosend/cli --help` works without a global install, but a reader following the README would not discover it. A second automation gap: the receipt link arrives by email, while the `--json` send response exposes the message id but not the receipt URL, so a script cannot close the loop without mailbox access.
- **Change I would make.** Add an `npx` quickstart to the README and expose the receipt URL (or a `receipt <message-id>` command) in the CLI's JSON output so a CI job can verify its own send.
```
